title: DC-area forecast: Pleasant streak lasts until Sunday rain
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: It’ll be hard to find a cloud in the sky this evening as temperatures settle through the 70s.

What’s next? Loads of sun and more 70s for Friday. Clouds increase through Saturday ahead of Saturday night and Sunday’s rain potential as the remnants of Hurricane Isaias pass by.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: It’ll stay mainly clear. Temperatures fall into the 60s after sunset on the way to lows ranging from the mid-40s to lower 50s. Winds of the day diminish through the night. Confidence: Medium-High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Friday): Mostly to partly sunny, and still quite delightful. It’s a touch cooler again, with highs mainly in the low and mid-70s. Winds are light. Confidence: Medium-High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: Partly cloudy skies are a good bet through the night. With that added cloud cover, temperatures are a touch milder than tonight, with lows mainly in the low and mid-50s. Confidence: Medium-High

A look ahead

Clouds increase through much of Saturday, starting partly cloudy and ending mostly cloudy as the remnants of Isaias make their way toward us. It should stay dry through the daylight period, with highs around 70 to 75. Some rain may arrive as soon as around 10 p.m. Saturday night, or as late as around 8 a.m. Sunday morning. Confidence: Medium

Periods of rain are likely Sunday. It probably won't rain nonstop, but it could rain at just about any time after sunrise. A wave or two could have embedded downpours, and if enough warm and unstable air makes it this far north, then we’ll have to monitor for a potential tornado threat late day or evening. Given the clouds and rain, highs probably get stuck in the 60s to near 70, but it could be rather humid. Confidence: Medium

A few showers could linger into Monday (Columbus Day), but we should trend drier and perhaps sunnier with time. As rain ends, highs should strive for 70 or a bit above. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for October 8

Tropical air in 2017 sent the overnight low to a record 75 degrees, creating unusually hot and humid October conditions more typical of midsummer.

Today’s daily digit — 9/10: Basically as awesome as yesterday, but a bit warmer and breezier. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.
